decision: Use two bounded, one-input/one-output evidence exporters: one in dom0 for persistent qrexec policy evidence and one under the dedicated non-root Coordinator-Qube service identity for service deployment evidence.

comparison.correctness: Preserves the real Qubes trust topology: dom0 never needs Coordinator-Qube filesystem access and the Coordinator Qube never needs dom0 policy access. Evidence is joined only by the existing artifact verifier.
comparison.robustnessSecurity: Each exporter has bounded input/output, constant non-diagnostic stderr, no shell, no MissionQueue mutation, and delegates path/identity/immutability checks to the existing hardened collectors.
comparison.latency: Only local file reads and JSON serialization; no additional qrexec round trip is introduced by evidence collection itself.
comparison.resourceUse: Process-per-call, bounded buffers, no daemon, watcher, database, WAL, or persistent service state.
comparison.regressionRisk: Adds thin adapters around existing collectors instead of a second evidence authority or changes to MissionQueue/WorkerRuntime.
comparison.qa: Host-only happy-path tests remain intentionally limited because canonical Qubes paths and kernel EUID binding must not be weakened for test convenience. Syntax and negative framing tests can run off-Qubes; successful collection must be qualified in the real trust domains.

rejected.reason: violates Qubes trust separation and creates unnecessary privilege/IPC surface
adds lifecycle, memory, IPC, and privileged attack surface without improving evidence correctness
would weaken canonical path and identity enforcement solely to make host tests easier

failuresLessons: A structurally correct artifact is not sufficient unless each trust domain produces its own evidence.
Do not make Qubes canonical-path or service-identity checks configurable in production just to improve host-test convenience.
Export failures must not reflect input, paths, credentials, MACs, keys, lease tokens, or stack traces.
safety: Read-only defensive qualification only; no real financial transactions, payment data, fraud workflow, or weakened security controls.
